trigger: reader arrives at a domain section by anchor link or search hit rather than from the top of the document
classification_rationale: Compounds doc-2. GitHub heading slugs derive from heading text, so adding the marker or retitling a row changes its slug: old links to RE-VERIFIED rows break to top-of-page where the banner is, while links to the 194 UNVERIFIED rows keep working and land the reader past the banner. The legend omits the marker, so the landed reader has no decoding key and a 2026-03-30 grade is presented indistinguishably from a re-verified one. Selection effect makes the failure mode systematically worse for exactly the rows least worth trusting.
summary: anchor links preferentially survive to stale rows and break on re-verified ones, so deep-linked readers bypass the scope banner

trigger: a future edit adds a row header shaped in one of six ways the awk mis-parses
classification_rationale: Tested against a synthetic fixture in the scratchpad, never the repo file. Six shapes mis-tally silently: a Partial row whose TITLE contains the text :white_check_mark: counts Done (first-match order); two icons counts Done; a header with no shortcode is dropped from the total with no error; Unicode icons are dropped (and the map's own 22.3 BODY already uses the Unicode style, so copying it into a header makes the row vanish); a ### N.M line inside a fenced code block is counted; ###1.7 or a leading space is dropped. happy-path verified the file has zero such lines today (265 rows, 0 no-icon, 0 double-icon, 0 no-tier, 0 in fences), so the published 195 23 47 265 is accurate - the exposure is the NEXT edit, and the Method advertises the awk as the reproduction procedure. E0 because it fires on edit with no actor and no configuration.
summary: the Method's awk mis-tallies six header shapes silently; correct today, but it is the advertised reproduction procedure with no guard

trigger: a single row regrade requires four coordinated hand edits and nothing checks them against each other
classification_rationale: The Method itself admits nothing in tests/ or CI checks the four hand-maintained views against the awk. Three of the four match today (headline bars, tier bars, per-domain table - independently confirmed by happy-path and consistency-auditor). unhappy-path reports the fourth as already divergent: caption at :1577 says 49 plugins (+2 planned) while the table carries 51 shipped rows and agents/plugins/ has 51 meson-built dirs. NOTE the direct contradiction with happy-path, which measured the same artefacts in the same wave and concluded the table has 53 rows = 51 + 2 planned and that 49 = 51 minus example minus chargen, matching the caption. Two same-wave reporters disagree on a countable fact; this must be settled by counting, not by preferring a reporter. The mechanism finding (one regrade, four edits, no cross-check) stands regardless and is the durable half.
summary: four hand-maintained views have no automated cross-check; reporters disagree on whether Appendix A's plugin count is already divergent

trigger: a later pass emits a finding_id prefix already used by an earlier pass, e.g. restarting UP-N at 1
classification_rationale: The read rule joins all rows sharing a finding_id into one supersession chain, so a reused id silently rewrites an unrelated still-open finding's disposition history - corruption of the governance evidence record, which is why the reporter derived I2. The reporter self-mitigated by numbering from UP-16 after inspecting the ledger. Orchestrator VERIFIED no collision exists: 101 rows, 67 distinct finding_ids, zero ids appearing in more than one pass_ordinal, zero pass-3 ids reusing a pass-1/2 id. Because the wrong OUTCOME is measured not to have occurred in this artefact, the row is recorded at SHOULD rather than BLOCKING for THIS run; the hazard itself is unguarded (nothing validates it) and belongs in a ledger validator. This is not a de-escalation of a live finding - the raising reporter and the orchestrator agree the collision did not happen - but the schema hazard is real and must not be read as closed by luck.
summary: reused finding_id across passes would silently rewrite an unrelated finding's history; verified not to have occurred here, unguarded in general

trigger: reader resolves a ledger row's line field against HEAD instead of against its reviewed_at_sha
classification_rationale: Two observations. First, g1-repro-1 was written directly as disposition fixed with no open predecessor - it is a verification ANCHOR rather than a finding, so recording it in a per-finding schema is a mild misuse, accepted knowingly. Second, 12 of 14 pass-1 open rows' line values now point at blank or unrelated lines at HEAD; SKILL.md:1705 states line is relative to reviewed_at_sha and drifts, so this is schema-conformant, but a reader without that rule sees dangling citations. Matches the standing memory that ledger line drift and unresolvable reviewed_at_sha are documented and accepted, graded INFO, never a block.
summary: a verification-anchor row recorded as fixed with no raising row, and pass-1 line anchors now dangling at HEAD - both schema-conformant

trigger: every pass appends its rows after the commit range it reviews, so no gate ever reviews the ledger
classification_rationale: The reviewed range ends at 4a4da796c where the ledger holds 82 rows; the working tree holds 101 across three later commits. Structurally, the ledger's own integrity is never inside a reviewed range, so no gate reads it for conformance unless explicitly tasked - as consistency-auditor was here, which is how cons-6 surfaced. Compounded by squash-merge collapsing the git ordering that corroborates the self-declared recorded_at precedence key.
summary: the ledger's rows always land outside the range they review, so its integrity is never gated by default

trigger: reader trusts an unmarked Done row in a security domain at the same weight as a re-verified one
classification_rationale: Projection from the measured sample, not a new row-level claim. Of the 71 re-verified rows about 16 changed grade (7 upward, 9 downward in e2b1ad8a0) - roughly a 23 percent correction rate, implying about 45 expected mis-grades among the 194 carry-overs, of which 20 unmarked Done rows sit in the security domains 9, 18 and 21. Corroborated independently: security-guardian sampled 11 unmarked security-relevant Done rows and 1 failed (sec-2), and consistency-auditor's hedge-word sweep independently failed a 12th (cons-2, 18.6 AD/Entra stub). So the projection is not hypothetical - two same-wave reporters each found a false Done without being shown the other's. Recorded at SHOULD per the PO ruling that general staleness is a follow-up; the two SPECIFIC false Dones gate on their own rows.
summary: measured 23 percent correction rate in the verified sample projects about 45 mis-grades among the 194 carry-overs, 20 of them Done rows in security domains

trigger: a governance or enterprise-readiness agent cites an unmarked Done row as closure evidence in a ledger row
classification_rationale: Evidence-laundering loop. The map is loaded as reference by governance agents - .claude/agents/architect.md:39 still describes it as 139-capability tracking, two baselines stale - and a Gate 6 agent citing an unmarked Done row records a ledger row whose epistemic_status is verified and whose file is the map rather than code. Because the ledger is append-only and carries no back-pointer to un-re-verified v3.0, the stale grade becomes durable governance evidence. doc-2 compounds it: the citing agent may never have seen the marker convention. Mitigant: the ledger's file field does say docs/capability-map.md, so a careful reader can tell the evidence is doc-sourced, which is why this is I3-adjacent rather than a clean I3.
summary: unmarked stale Done rows can be laundered into the governance ledger as verified evidence with no back-pointer to their v3.0 provenance

trigger: a future edit records verification in body prose using any of the four in-body phrasings instead of the exact marker string
classification_rationale: The marker vocabulary is already forked: 27 in-body mentions use verified 2026-09-07, Re-verified, Corrected 2026-09-08 or regraded 2026-09-07, while only the exact string *(verified 2026-09-07)* is counted by the Method's grep, which is how 73 reconciles as 71 rows plus the Method self-citation plus the Appendix A caption. Consequence: a row Corrected 2026-09-08 is FRESHER than a row verified 09-07 yet reads as unverified to the grep. Independently corroborated - doc-1 and cons-5 found the under-marked rows from the opposite direction (six in total across the two reporters, neither shown the other's list), and doc-3 found the date fork. Root cause shared with doc-1, doc-3 and cons-5; fix once.
summary: four competing in-body verification phrasings against one counted marker string, so freshness and the published 73/71 reconciliation diverge

trigger: reader plans a zero-dependency server deployment from the parity plan's architectural-comparison section
classification_rationale: FACTS-VERSUS-LABEL DISAGREEMENT, recorded per the stronger-of rule and referred for adjudication - NOT settled by the orchestrator. Reporter recorded I4 with E3 and then labelled the finding SHOULD; I4 has base HIGH and E3 is neutral, so the stated facts derive HIGH while the label's floor is MEDIUM, and the rule reads the finding at the stronger of the two and reports the disagreement. Reporter's evidence: enterprise-parity-plan.md:16, :30 and :74 advertise SQLite embedded zero-ops server storage while ADR-0006 makes the server fail closed at boot without a Postgres DSN. Orchestrator counter-evidence, recorded so the adjudicator sees both sides: the file is Status Draft dated 2026-03-30, :16 sits in a comparison column explicitly headed Yuzu v0.7.0, and the document already carries phase-level supersession notes (e.g. :276-284 for ADR-0024) - which supports I8 diagnosable-and-visible rather than I4 concealing, since a fail-closed boot is a loud error. Referred to enterprise-readiness at Gate 6 for an independent I4-versus-I8 call; the orchestrator is not the adjudicator and did not lower the band.
summary: parity plan advertises SQLite zero-ops server storage against ADR-0006 fail-closed Postgres; I4-vs-I8 derivation disputed, referred to Gate 6

trigger: operator relies on Guardian drift evidence being retained and replayed after an agent-server disconnect
classification_rationale: Third Guardian statement defect and the most serious, because 31.8 CARRIES the *(verified 2026-09-07)* marker - a row asserted as re-verified this pass is wrong. 31.8 at :1318 says queued events flush when the server returns; 31.7 at :1314 says the legacy path drains no event queue and has no push. The code is a third thing: the legacy path DOES push live via emit_guardian_event (agent.cpp:3378-3387, __guard__/event) but DROPS on no stream (guardian_engine.cpp:940, comment drop; durable buffering is A3), and the only retain-and-retry outbox is Spark-gated with prefer_spark_ false. So the two rows are wrong in OPPOSITE directions and 32's preamble contradicts 31.7 as well. I6 raises to HIGH under FALSE ASSURANCE: offline retention of drift evidence is a data-integrity and audit-evidence control on the security-enforcement subsystem, advertised as in force and not enforced. Must be folded with sec-1 as one Guardian correction: 31.7 states live push plus drop-when-offline; 31.8 deletes the flush sentence.
summary: 31.8 (a marked re-verified row) claims queued Guardian events flush on reconnect; the legacy path drops them, and the durable outbox is Spark-gated

trigger: reader or questionnaire responder treats 18.6 Active Directory / Entra Integration as a shipped identity integration
classification_rationale: Unmarked v3.0 carry-over graded Done whose own body says LDAP sync stub and full LDAP support planned; directory_sync.hpp:207-208 and directory_sync.cpp:973 confirm the AD/LDAP half is a stub. The Entra half ships, so the title over-scopes rather than being wholly false - reporter's recommendation is regrade to Partial or retitle to Entra Integration. RECORDED AT THE REPORTER'S DERIVATION AND REFERRED: the reporter applied I6 base MEDIUM without the FALSE ASSURANCE raise. Whether an identity-integration control counts as security-relevant for that raise - which would make it HIGH and bring it inside the PO's carve-out that a sampled false Done for a security-relevant control gates - is referred to compliance-officer at Gate 6. The orchestrator is not the adjudicator and has neither raised nor lowered the band.
summary: 18.6 AD/Entra graded Done while its own body and directory_sync confirm the AD/LDAP half is a stub; false-assurance raise referred to Gate 6

trigger: reader compares 30.4's stated policy evaluation cadence against 16's preamble
classification_rationale: 30.4 says PolicyStore (16) with a typical 5-minute cadence; 16's preamble at :773 says a 3600-second default, and policy_evaluator.hpp:107 confirms default_interval_seconds 3600. Internal contradiction on a number the same document states twice. Adjacent to sec-2 and UP-16, which are about which TRIGGER TYPES are evaluated - this one is about the interval value and is a separate defect at a separate line, so it is not clustered with them.
summary: 30.4 states a typical 5-minute policy cadence against 16's and the code's 3600-second default

trigger: reader treats 30.3 Done as covering all three surfaces the row names
classification_rationale: 30.3 is graded Done while its own body defers Policy fromResultSet: to PR-E2, and policy_store.cpp:593-595 rejects that surface at create. One of the row's three named surfaces is not merely unimplemented but actively refused. The defect is disclosed in the row body, so a careful reader is not misled - hence LOW rather than a false-assurance raise. Regrade to Partial or narrow the title.
summary: 30.3 graded Done although one of its three named surfaces is rejected at create by policy_store.cpp:593-595

trigger: reader uses header-marker presence to bound which rows were re-verified
classification_rationale: Marker-parity sweep in both directions. Under-marked: 8.3 at :431 carries an in-body Re-verified 2026-09-07 note with no header marker - a SIXTH such row beyond the five in doc-1, found independently (neither reporter was shown the other's list, same wave). Over-marked direction came back clean: 31.4 and 31.5 are marked with byte-identical bodies, and 31.4's observe-only claim still holds at guard_systemd.cpp:14-15, so the marking is legitimate. 20.7, 21.5 and 24.10 diffs are header-split artefacts, not edits. Fold into doc-1 as one correction covering six rows.
summary: 8.3 is a sixth under-marked row carrying in-body 2026-09-07 verification without a header marker; the over-marked direction is clean

trigger: fold commits claim to resolve findings without appending the corresponding terminal supersession rows
classification_rationale: Two ledger-hygiene defects. First, at HEAD six BLOCKING raise rows (sec-H1, sec-H2, UP-1, sre-H1, EA-H1, comp-C1) plus seven SHOULD and five NICE have no terminal supersession although a43c6a467, e2b1ad8a0 and 4a4da796c claim to fold them - SKILL.md requires the append on the same push that makes the claim, and the schema states open is not a resting place. Orchestrator independently measured the same thing before seeing this report by computing the field-wise last-write-wins live view: 34 rows live-open, including exactly those six BLOCKING ids - independent_reporters 2. Second, all 32 existing supersessions share recorded_at with their raise row, so the declared precedence key ties and ordering silently falls back to file position. Both are fixed by appending terminal rows with DISTINCT timestamps, which every pass-3 row does. The park check is clean: jq -e exit 4 on both the committed file and the working tree.
summary: six BLOCKING and twelve lesser raise rows never superseded despite fold commits claiming closure; all 32 prior supersessions tie on recorded_at

trigger: reader compares the map, the roadmap and the ADR-1005 execution plan on the same facts
classification_rationale: Three cross-document divergences, each with its owning document named so the fix lands in one place. roadmap.md:1103 grades 9.8 Open with no note while the map grades 26.3 Partial (owner: roadmap). roadmap.md:1010 still specifies ConnectorStore (SQLite) against ADR-0006's new-server-stores-default-to-Postgres rule (owner: roadmap; independently noted by architect as arch-4's tail). adr-1005-execution-plan.md:99 says a roughly 50-tool surface where the actual count is 91 (owner: exec plan). Positive result on the same sweep: 24.8's 91-tool claim re-counted by its own cited awk gives 91, and the A5 Today block plus open issue #2990 agree with the map - EA-H1's fold is sound.
summary: three cross-document divergences owned by the roadmap and the ADR-1005 exec plan, not by the map; 24.8's 91-tool claim independently re-confirmed

classification_rationale: CORRECTION, not a refutation of the finding - the defect stands, one of its two claims does not. Two same-wave reporters disagreed on a countable fact, so the orchestrator counted rather than preferring a reporter. Measured: Appendix A's table body has 53 rows; grep -c Planned = 2; rows matching example or chargen = 2, both labelled Test/Debug; 53 minus 2 planned minus 2 test/debug = 49, exactly matching the :1577 caption 49 plugins (+ 2 planned); ls -d agents/plugins/*/ = 51 = 49 shipped + example + chargen. unhappy-path's sub-claim that the caption is ALREADY divergent is therefore false - it counted the 51 shipped table rows without subtracting the two Test/Debug rows. happy-path and docs-writer each reached 49 independently in the same wave. The MECHANISM half stands untouched and is why this row remains open: one regrade still requires four coordinated hand edits with no automated cross-check, a gap the Method paragraph itself admits. Band and gate unchanged (NICE/I8 before and after), so this is a correction rather than a de-escalation and needs no adjudicator; per the skill, a real finding whose citation is wrong is corrected, never refuted, so the kill shape is not recorded against the defect.
summary: corrected: Appendix A's 49-plugin caption is right (53 = 49 + 2 test/debug + 2 planned); only the no-cross-check mechanism half of UP-20 stands

trigger: Gate 5 ran because both unhappy-path and consistency-auditor produced findings
classification_rationale: Gate 5 design record, not a defect. Seven scenarios CH-1..CH-7. CH-1 (UP-16/sec-2) and CH-2 (cons-1/sec-1) are the only two that block this push, and both block via their UNDERLYING HIGH finding rather than via the scenario - P0 is a planning label, not a gate. Chaos independently re-read and confirmed the two dispositive code sites without being asked to take them on trust: guardian_engine.cpp:940 returns and drops with the comment that durable buffering is A3, and policy_store.cpp:1247-1249 is the interval-only LEFT JOIN. It records that the code read is DISPOSITIVE for both corrections, so no runtime run is required to authorise them; CH-2 on the UAT rig is reserved for the case where the author disputes the drop. CH-3 (cons-2) is verify-by-code-read sufficient. CH-4/5/6/7 are follow-ups. The scope decision explicitly recommends AGAINST any chaos harness, container or scheduled job for a markdown file, naming a roughly 20-line pre-commit lint plus a single marker vocabulary as the correct control - and CH-5 notes that one mechanical sweep adding a per-row v3.0 carry-over marker to the 194 unmarked rows would collapse UP-18, UP-24, UP-25 and UP-26 into a single fix.
summary: Gate 5 chaos design CH-1..CH-7 produced; two blocking scenarios both resolvable by doc correction, harness explicitly not recommended

trigger: a43c6a467 states it folds six BLOCKING findings but appends no terminal supersession row for any of them
classification_rationale: compliance-officer's adjudication of cons-6 as an EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY gap rather than hygiene, invoking the standing rule that SOC-2 evidence-integrity gaps are a firm HIGH and are not to be soft-pedalled. Six pass-1 rows recorded severity_mapped BLOCKING (sec-H1, sec-H2, UP-1, sre-H1, EA-H1, comp-C1, all recorded_at 2026-09-07T13:30:54Z) have NO later row at all, so their live disposition is open, while commit a43c6a467's message asserts closure. The CC8.1 change-management record therefore shows six blocking findings raised and never resolved, and a reader who is not the producer cannot tell from the ledger which of the two artefacts is true - which is precisely the property SOC 2 CC8.1 requires of change-management evidence. I1 because governance.d IS the change-management control here and it does not hold; E0 because it fires on the fold with no actor. Three independent reporters: consistency-auditor raised it as cons-6, the orchestrator measured the same six ids by computing the field-wise last-write-wins live view before seeing that report, and compliance-officer re-derived it and supplied the band. Resolution is mechanical and lands in this run at Gate 6b: one terminal row per id citing the fixing commit, with distinct recorded_at values.
summary: six BLOCKING ledger rows have no terminal supersession while the fold commit claims closure - a CC8.1 change-management evidence-integrity gap

trigger: incident responder or agentic worker relies on the audit row to reconstruct which devices an enforcement chain skipped
classification_rationale: 30.2, an unmarked v3.0 carry-over graded Done, claims stale result-set members (offline over 24h, decommissioned, removed from management group) are silently dropped at resolve time WITH a dashboard-surfaced warning AND that the audit row records the dropped IDs for forensic completeness. None of it exists. The resolve path at agent_registry.cpp:1405-1463 preloads owner-checked membership and a member absent from the live registry simply fails to match - no 24h rule, no warning, no audit row. Measured: grep for the result_set audit verbs across server/core/src/*.cpp yields only access, create, delete, pin, unpin; grep for dropped_ids or dropped_members yields 0. The text is a verbatim restatement of docs/scope-walking-design.md 4.3, which is DESIGN, not shipped, while result_set_store.cpp:590 states the real contract as stale members drop silently, full stop. I6 raises to HIGH under FALSE ASSURANCE: a forensic-completeness AUDIT guarantee is advertised as in force and is not enforced - the same defect class as cons-1. This is a false Done on an audit control, so it falls inside the PO carve-out to the unmarked-row staleness ruling rather than outside it.
summary: 30.2 claims a dropped-ID audit row and dashboard warning for forensic completeness; neither the audit verb nor the warning exists in code

trigger: a sales engineer or auditor lifts a single unmarked Done row into a CAIQ answer or a Workstream G evidence packet
classification_rationale: The banner at :3 and the Method at :41-49 scope the partial re-baseline correctly, but the 194 carry-over rows carry no per-row marker, so a row lifted out of context arrives as an unqualified Done. Absence rests on required-doc item 5 by analogy - the evidence index the change's contract touches - and on the customer-assurance workstream at docs/enterprise-readiness-soc2-first-customer.md:498-511. Independently reported: docs-writer reached the same conclusion from the legend-table direction as doc-2 and enterprise-readiness reached it from the questionnaire-copy direction, neither having been shown the other. Minimum disclosure named by the reporter: a per-row v3.0-grade tag or an evidence-grade column, plus a verify-against-code-before-citing rule in the Workstream A evidence index. This is the same fix Gate 5 CH-5 proposes and enterprise-readiness endorsed as proportionate.
summary: the partial-re-baseline disclosure does not travel with an individual row, so a carry-over Done lifted into a questionnaire arrives unqualified

trigger: auditor asks who changed a given row's grade, when, and on what evidence
classification_rationale: Split verdict. For the roughly 105 REGRADED rows, git blame plus the inline citation plus the date marker plus the ledger's finding_id to file:line mapping reconstructs who, when and on what evidence - change-traceability is adequate. For the CARRY-OVER rows the only anchor is the v3.0 commit, and the map carries no back-pointer to ledger ids in either direction. Recorded as LOW because the regraded half - which is what this change actually did - is traceable; the carry-over half folds into comp-2's fix.
summary: regraded rows are traceable via blame, citation and ledger; carry-over rows anchor only to the v3.0 commit and the map has no ledger back-pointer

trigger: reader plans a TLS posture from 18.9's description of the HTTPS flag
classification_rationale: 18.9 describes an opt-in --https flag; main.cpp:767-778 shows HTTPS is the DEFAULT with --no-https as the opt-out. The row is stale in the CONSERVATIVE direction - the shipped control is stronger than advertised - so there is no false assurance and no wrong operational outcome, only an understated posture. Independently corroborated: security-guardian's Gate 2 sample independently classified 18.9 as stale-safe for the same reason without having been shown this finding.
summary: 18.9 describes HTTPS as opt-in via --https; it is default-on with --no-https opt-out, so the row understates the shipped control

trigger: reader counts RBAC securable types from 18.3
classification_rationale: 18.3 says 10 securable types; rbac_store.cpp:559 seeds 27. Understated, so the control holds and no reader is misled about enforcement - only about breadth. Independently corroborated by security-guardian's Gate 2 sample, which classified 18.3 stale-safe on the same 27-versus-10 observation without being shown this finding.
summary: 18.3 says 10 RBAC securable types where rbac_store seeds 27 - understated, control unaffected

trigger: operator writes a Prometheus alert rule on the yuzu_result_set_resolve_seconds histogram
classification_rationale: 30.4 contradicts itself within one row: its first sentence lists yuzu_result_set_resolve_seconds as Remaining, its fifth lists the same histogram among metrics that surface health and runaway-script detection. Measured: grep -rl for the metric name across server and agents returns 0 files, while the other four named metrics do exist (server.cpp:18635, :18655, :18796 and rest_api_v1.cpp:7857). Band LOW because the row itself discloses the metric is Remaining, so a careful reader is warned - the defect is the internal contradiction, not a clean false claim.
summary: 30.4 lists yuzu_result_set_resolve_seconds both as Remaining and as a shipped metric; it exists in no source file

trigger: SIEM integrator or capacity planner designs against webhook and offload event fan-out
classification_rationale: 21.4 says async delivery on detached threads with a 10-concurrent-delivery semaphore; webhook_store.hpp:210 is a bounded StoreWorkerPool of 4 by 256 with overflow dropped. Neither 21.4 nor 21.3 discloses that event fan-out is best-effort - drop on queue-full, no retry, in-memory batch lost on crash - which is exactly the property a downstream SIEM integrator plans against. Not raised to false assurance because neither row claims durability or at-least-once in the first place; the defect is an omission plus a wrong concurrency mechanism, not an advertised guarantee that fails. sre's wider sweep found 12 durability-claiming rows, verified 11, and this is the only stale-but-not-false one - the single outright failure was sre-1.
summary: 21.4 describes a 10-concurrent semaphore where the code is a bounded 4x256 pool with drop-on-overflow; best-effort fan-out is undisclosed in 21.3 and 21.4

trigger: reader takes the Yuzu v0.7.0 comparison column as a current statement of the storage substrate
classification_rationale: The substantive residue of UP-27 after adjudication. enterprise-parity-plan.md:16, :30 and :643 state SQLite embedded WAL-mode zero-ops server storage, which is wrong against ADR-0006. Recorded at LOW rather than HIGH because the adjudicator established the failure is visible and diagnosable, not concealing - see the UP-27 supersession. Recommended fix is a supersession callout in the same pattern the document already uses at :276-284 for ADR-0024, pointing at ADR-0006/0007, on each of the three lines. Out of range - this file is not in the reviewed diff.
summary: parity plan's three SQLite zero-ops server-storage lines need an ADR-0006 supersession callout in the pattern the file already uses

trigger: prospect evaluates the database dependency from 2.6 while 38.4 states the opposite
classification_rationale: Same defect as arch-2, reached independently from the procurement angle rather than the migration-ladder angle: 2.6 says InstructionStore is stored in SQLite while the map's own census at :1494 says zero SQLite-only server stores remain. enterprise-readiness adds the reason it matters commercially - database dependency is a standard procurement question, so a self-contradiction on that axis is the one most likely to be noticed by a prospect. Two independent reporters (architect at Gate 3, enterprise-readiness at Gate 6, neither shown the other's finding). Fix is one word plus the CH-5 marker.
summary: 2.6's SQLite claim contradicts the map's own zero-SQLite-server-stores census on the axis procurement asks about

trigger: the 74 percent headline is quoted without the Method paragraph travelling with it
classification_rationale: 74 percent is defensible only as an UPPER BOUND with its qualification on the same line, never as a bare figure. Three converging reasons: the verified sample moved nine rows down against four up; arch-1's double-count puts the true figure at 194/264 = 73 percent; and CLAUDE.md:106's overstated caveat was independently ruled still TRUE by architect. Recorded at I8 rather than I3 because the Method DOES make the figure diagnosable to anyone who reads it - the defect is that the qualification does not travel, which is comp-2's mechanism applied to the headline. Reporter supplied exact replacement wording for the line adjacent to the bar.
summary: 74 percent is defensible only as an upper bound with its scope qualification on the same line as the bar

trigger: a customer who read v3.0 tries to determine what changed grade in v4.0
classification_rationale: No consolidated record of what was regraded between v3.0 and v4.0. The nine e2b1ad8a0 downgrades - 5.2 Process Termination, 5.4 Service Control, 7.4 Software Uninstall, 10.5 File Deletion, 12.2 and 12.3 WMI, 13.4 HTTP POST to Not Started; 7.6 Deployment and 18.8 Device Authorization Tokens to Partial - were never advertised in the operator manual (docs/user-manual/agent-plugins.md carries no kill, stop-service, uninstall or delete-file action) and CHANGELOG.md never claimed them, so no explicit customer promise was broken. BUT they stood as Done in the map since v3.0 on 2026-03-30, roughly five months, and README.md:251 presents the map as the live capability inventory - so any prospect who read it was told they shipped. 18.8 Device Authorization Tokens is the one security-relevant member of that set. Not a required-doc absence under the six-item list; recorded as a customer-assurance gap with a concrete fix - a nine-row old-to-new regrade table in the Method or an appendix.
summary: no v3.0-to-v4.0 regrade record; nine rows stood as Done for five months in the document README calls the live capability inventory

adjudicated_by: enterprise-readiness (Gate 6) - not the change's author, not the reporting agent, and not the party that argued the de-escalation; separation in force is the de-escalation rule's
adjudication_rationale: DE-ESCALATION from BLOCKING to NICE, band-moving, so it carries an independent adjudicator per the de-escalation rule. The referred question was whether the parity plan's SQLite zero-ops claim is I4 or I8. I4 requires guidance that names an action which causes damage OR that fails in a way which CONCEALS the real state, and its own carve-out excludes guidance that merely fails visibly and diagnosably. The adjudicator resolved it against the code: a server started per that document without a DSN hits server.cpp:3926 and prints 'Refusing to start: no PostgreSQL DSN. Set --postgres-dsn / YUZU_POSTGRES_DSN (ADR-0006/0007 ...)', with main.cpp:1291 warning earlier. Nothing is written, nothing is concealed, and the remedy is named in the error text - squarely the carve-out. Supporting context: the file is Status Draft dated 2026-03-30, :16 sits in a column headed Yuzu v0.7.0, it is untouched by this range, and it is linked from neither README.md nor the site nav. Residual risk is a pre-sales expectation error, not an operator-damage path. Facts restated to I8/E3 so the label and the facts agree; the substantive fix survives as ea-1.
summary: adjudicated I8 not I4 - the fail-closed boot names its own remedy, so the failure is visible and diagnosable; de-escalated BLOCKING to NICE
